# Agents and models

- **Hand a task to the cheapest model whose mistake would be caught before it lands.** The
  full split is the `model-delegation` skill. *(2026-10-11-cheap-reviews-catch-real-bugs)*
- **Tell a reviewer which commands it may run.** Read-only is about edits, not output: a
  suite or build in your worktree rewrites what a running gate reads. Or give it its own
  worktree. *(2026-10-18-reviewers-must-not-build-in-your-worktree)*
- **Review every commit before pushing it.** Review read-only, on a mid-size model, with a
  fixed brief: correctness and safety, `file:line`, a concrete scenario, a word cap. The
  `cheap-reviewer` subagent does exactly this. Verify each finding before acting on it.
  *(2026-10-11-cheap-reviews-catch-real-bugs)*
- **Agents that share a stack, a database or rate limits run one at a time.**
  *(2026-10-11-second-stack-reloads-pages)*
- **Before shipping a skill or tool, have an agent use it inside a copy of the user's
  environment.** No network, only the platform's documented libraries, only the unzipped
  package, and a real user prompt. Read its reply, its files and what it had to guess. Check
  the platform's size limits first.
  *(2026-10-18-simulate-the-users-sandbox-before-shipping-a-skill)*
- **State the user's job in one line before planning a server, auth or storage.** Then
  list the lightest paths first: what ships, what a sibling project did, what the client
  does natively. Plan only for the gap, and name it.
  *(2026-10-18-state-the-job-before-planning-a-server)*
- **Ask for work that survives being cut short.** Agents share the session's limits: have
  them write findings as they go, push after every green commit, resume rather than restart,
  and clean up. After one stops, check each worktree against its remote.
  *(2026-10-11-background-agents-hit-usage-limits)*
  *(2026-10-18-check-worktrees-after-an-agent-stops)*
- **Fetch with no cookies to see what an AI client gets; content behind a sign-in is
  invisible to it.** For a private site, the user carries content in (a skill, an archive)
  or shares a scoped, expiring read link, which anyone holding it can use.
  *(2026-10-18-check-what-an-ai-fetcher-receives)*
- **Scope a batch with a cheap read-only pass before delegating it.** A plan written from
  item names hides items that differ in kind, are already done, or depend on something
  missing. *(2026-10-11-scope-a-batch-before-delegating-it)*
